assertions.description: The GamepadButton interface the attribute extends is exposed on Window.
GamepadButton.prototype has the new readonly type attribute (the exact surface this feature ships; requires the GamepadButtonTypes flag in Chrome 152).
type is defined as a readonly accessor (getter, no setter) on the prototype, per WebIDL readonly attribute semantics.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof GamepadButton === 'undefined') return false; const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(GamepadButton.prototype, 'type'); return !!d && typeof d.get === 'function' && d.set === undefined; })()

assertions.description: navigator.getGamepads is a function — the entry point the classification is read through (part of this feature's usage contract, not a generic baseline check: the demo's polling loop calls exactly this).
On a connected pad every button.type value is one of the spec enum strings standard / non-standard / trackpad — new unknown values must not appear.
assertions.test: Requires a physical gamepad plus a button press (user activation) before getGamepads() exposes the pad; then verify each button.type ∈ {standard, non-standard, trackpad} on the live console demo.

assertions.description: A controller with an integrated touchpad (DualShock 4 / DualSense) reports exactly one button with type 'trackpad'.
assertions.test: Requires touchpad-equipped hardware: connect a DualShock 4 or DualSense, press a button, and confirm the touchpad click reports type 'trackpad' in the live console demo.
